messages:
maria: Quick design check — finalizing copy + a11y for the eval run modal. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz (see right panel). I sketched two CTA options: `Run suite` (primary) + `Quick run` (secondary) or single CTA `Run tests`. Thoughts on clarity vs accidental runs? jay: I prefer `Run suite` — clearer that it runs multiple tests. but can we add a small secondary line: 'This will run N prompts · ~2m' so people know cost/latency. oliver: +1 for showing cost/time. Also thinking about a confirmation step if a suite is >1000 prompts? accidental runs are expensive for users. Maybe a checkbox "I understand this will consume credits" for big runs. kira: Accessibility nits: contrast on the secondary button is below AA in the mock (text on #f3f5f7 bg). Also focus ring gets lost with our dark theme. We should ensure focus order: close X -> details link -> CTA -> cancel. Right now the close X is after the CTA in DOM. design-bot: automated-lint: color-contrast failure on element .modal-footer .secondary-btn (contrast 3.9:1). Recommend darkening to #475569 or increasing weight. maria: Good catch. Proposed copy + microcopy: primary: `Run suite` (aria-label="Run the selected test suite"), helper line: "Estimated time: ~2m · Estimated cost: $0.05" (small, muted). For large suites show inline warning: "This run will process 1,200 prompts and may take ~30m — charges apply." jay: For keyboard users we should add an explicit keyboard shortcut hint in the modal header: "Press R to run" and ensure that `R` doesn't conflict with other shortcuts in the console. Also confirm Escape closes the modal and returns focus to the originating Run button. kira: Suggest adding `aria-live="polite"` to the helper line so screen reader users get the ETA/cost announcement when the modal opens. Also add `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` and a visible focus trap. For reduced motion preference, avoid long animated progress bars. oliver: Regarding the confirmation for big runs — can we make it conditional? e.g., show checkbox only when prompts_count > 500 OR estimated_cost > $5. That avoids friction for small runs. Also log event `eval.run_confirm_shown` and `eval.run_confirm_accepted` for analytics. maria: Implementation snippet to add to the modal container: ```html

Estimated time: ~2m · Estimated cost: $0.05

``` Thoughts? jay: LGTM. for telemetry use names like `eval_run_initiated` and `eval_run_confirmation` and include properties: suite_id, prompts_count, estimated_cost_usd. we'll ask data infra to map. kira: A couple copy nits: change helper line to sentence-case: "Estimated time: ~2m · Estimated cost: $0.05" (your version had all caps in figma). For the big-run warning, use plain language: "This run will process 1,200 prompts and may take about 30 minutes. Estimated cost: $12.00." Avoid parentheses. maria: Noted. UX flow decision: show secondary "Quick run" option that only runs a single sample subset (5 prompts) for instant preview. That keeps a low-friction path. Will the team be okay adding another endpoint param `preview=true`? jay: Backend should support it. Add analytics `eval_run_preview_used`. Also show a tiny badge on the quick-run button: `Preview` in case it's ambiguous. kira: Final a11y checklist before handoff: 1) color contrast AA 2) focus trap verified with keyboard 3) screen reader announces ETA + cost on open 4) cancel/close target size >=44px 5) reduced-motion respected. If we get these, accessibility sign-off is quick. maria: Perfect. I'll update figma and push a dev ticket with all copy + aria attrs + telemetry props. @jay @kira @oliver please quick-react with :thumbsup: if you approve or drop comments if not. Thanks! :sparkles:
